The track is 25 mm of tape, so sensors should span somewhat more than the tape width to keep a reading on the line through small offsets, and they should sit ahead of the axle so the controller sees the line before the wheels reach it. Five sensors at 10 mm pitch (x = -0.02 to +0.02) give a span of 40 mm, with 12 mm footprints overlapping neighbours so the sum of readings stays above the 0.05 line-loss threshold and the signal stays continuous. Placing the row at y = 0.05 m gives roughly 5 cm of lookahead, which helps at speed. Wheel track 0.12 m and a 0.03 m wheel radius are mid-range, giving a stable yaw response without excessive turn inertia. Body width 0.12 m keeps the off-track limit at max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) = 0.06 m, a comfortable margin. Mass 0.7 kg is light enough to accelerate to about 1.5 m/s on a 7.4 V pack while keeping traction. I expect the robot to complete the oval and s-bend with few line losses, and I expect the slalom to be the hardest case because of its sharp direction changes.
